security_spec.violation_condition: OpenSBI saves/restores mstatus during HSM suspend/resume or context switch without preserving the MIPU/SIPU state bits, or inadvertently clears these bits during mstatus writes in init/trap handling, causing the automatic interrupt stacking behavior to be silently disabled after a context switch or resume
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: CSR write to mstatus that uses a hardcoded immediate mask (e.g., csrw mstatus, csrs mstatus, csrrc mstatus) without reading back MIPU/SIPU bit positions, or save/restore of mstatus in context_switch/HSM suspend-resume that omits newly defined status bits
security_spec.summary: Unpreserved MIPU/SIPU bits across OpenSBI mstatus save/restore silently disable automatic interrupt stacking, degrading fast-interrupt guarantees after HSM resume

findings.finding: mstatus_init() writes CSR_MSTATUS with a hardcoded value initialized to zero, setting only FS/VS bits. This is a blind csrw that destroys ALL other mstatus bits including any MIPU/SIPU state bits defined by the Smip extension. After this write, the automatic interrupt stacking behavior controlled by MIPU/SIPU would be silently disabled.

sbi_hart_reinit() calls mstatus_init(scratch) at line 715, which does the destructive hardcoded mstatus write (see above). This function is the reinitialization path called during warm resume from non-retentive suspend (via init_warm_resume). After resume, the MIPU/SIPU state bits are guaranteed to be cleared.

init_warm_resume() is the HSM warm-resume path. It calls sbi_hart_reinit() -> mstatus_init() which performs a destructive csr_write to mstatus. MIPU/SIPU state bits present before suspend are zeroed on resume; the automatic interrupt stacking behavior is silently lost after every non-retentive suspend/resume cycle.

No MSTATUS_MIPU or MSTATUS_SIPU bit definitions exist in the encoding header. The entire codebase has zero awareness of the Smip extension's state bits. Without these constants, save/restore macros and context-switch routines cannot reference the bits even if a developer wanted to preserve them.

sbi_hart_switch_mode() uses a read-modify-write pattern: csr_read CSR_MSTATUS, INSERT_FIELD to modify only MPP/MPIE/MPV, then csr_write back. This preserves all other mstatus bits including any future MIPU/SIPU bits because the register value is read first rather than using a hardcoded immediate.

Domain context switch saves and restores the entire sbi_trap_context (which includes mstatus) via sbi_memcpy of the full struct. All mstatus bits including any MIPU/SIPU bits are implicitly preserved through this complete copy.

TRAP_RESTORE_MEPC_MSTATUS restores mstatus by loading the full saved value from the trap register frame and writing it via csrw CSR_MSTATUS. Since the save path (TRAP_SAVE_MEPC_MSTATUS) captured the full CSR value, the round-trip preserves all bits including any MIPU/SIPU.
findings.snippet:
REG_L   t0, SBI_TRAP_REGS_OFFSET(mstatus)(a0)
csrw    CSR_MSTATUS, t0

findings.finding: HSM non-retentive suspend save saves mie, mip, medeleg, mideleg, menvcfg but does NOT explicitly save mstatus. While mstatus is preserved indirectly through the trap context save/restore chain, there is no explicit save here. If the warm-boot path reinitializes mstatus (which it does, via mstatus_init), there is no explicit restore of mstatus values, and the MIPU/SIPU bits would be lost.
